pages.title: Ponds: The Basics
pages.text: Place still water source blocks by the field; one cell serves $(thing)10$() planted plots and the 6 AM settlement draws a few cells based on usage.$(li)$(crop)Good for$(): small to medium fields, early game, a vanilla-style farm.$(li)$(warn)Upkeep$(): refill the drawn cells every day, or let a farm-mode maid handle it.$(br2)A bigger pond is more forgiving - extra cells give you buffer instead of matching plot counts exactly.

pages.title: Irrigator: Automation
pages.text: Holds $(thing)100 buckets$() and, once powered by redstone, waters the nearest $(thing)20$() plots within a radius of 8; one bucket lasts 2 MC days. Pipes on top refill it automatically, and a full tank runs for a very long time.$(li)$(crop)Good for$(): large fields, pipe and redstone automation.$(li)$(warn)Upkeep$(): it needs power and water, and each machine serves its own nearest plots - for a huge field place several at staggered spots.

pages.title: Rain & Cauldrons
pages.text: $(info)Rain relief$(): after $(thing)12 in-game hours$() of continuous rain, exposed crops grow with no water block at all - a free watering every so often. Snow does not count, roofs and leaves block it, and it ends when the rain stops.$(br2)$(info)Cauldron rain collection$(): an exposed cauldron slowly fills during rain and you can scoop from it with a bucket or bottle, a water supply that $(bold)costs no water blocks$(). Water inside a cauldron is not a source, though, and never waters farmland.$(br2)Easiest setup: a pond or irrigator as the baseline, rain as a bonus, and a cauldron of emergency water.
